messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 🔥 hosted-runtime-usw2: kvcache OOM surge detected (OOMs on worker pool rwd-hosted-rt-std). Error rate increased from 0.4% -> 8.2% in last 3m. Suspected cause: runaway context windows + continuous-batching regression. Paging on-call. https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/4378901234
maria (oncall): I'm on it. first check: is this isolated to a subset of models or global?
jon (sre): Logs show a big tail of requests with 'context_length' ~1.2M tokens hitting KV prefetch path. Many sessions never evict. Continuous batching metrics correlate: batch_size spike at same time.
ashley (runtime): I see a config rollout 2026-03-14T02:10 that increased batching.lookahead_ms and disabled conservative prefetch heuristics. That could amplify prefixes across sessions. Rolling back that flag will probably reduce aggregation.
maria (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle prefetch at gateway; 2) revert batching rollout; 3) enable aggressive eviction cap per-session. Which is fastest?
ryan (eng-runtime): Reverting the flag requires a canary rollback (takes ~6-8min). Gateway throttle can be patched in <3m via feature flag. I can push a blocking throttle to reduce prefetch width to 128 tokens and cap kv_window to 64k entries.
luis (prod-eng): Customer-facing impact: support queue shows ~15 customers reporting high latencies and 500s for generation endpoints. Marking P1 for hosted runtime customers on us-west-2. CS notified.
emily (support): Notifying top affected customers now. Using template: "We're seeing elevated errors for generation in us-west-2; engineers are working on mitigation. We'll update in 30m."
cs-notify-bot: Posted to customers.ping: "Hosted inference in us-west-2 experiencing transient errors; engineers investigating."
maria (oncall): OK, do the quick throttle. ryan, please apply gateway flag and keep us posted. ashley try to stage rollback in parallel.
ryan (eng-runtime): Applying flag now: PATCH /flags/runtime.prefetch.max_prefix_tokens = 128, /flags/runtime.kv.max_session_entries = 65536
ryan (eng-runtime): Command: ```
curl -X PATCH https://ff.redwood.internal/flags/runtime -d '{"prefetch.max_prefix_tokens":128,"kv.max_session_entries":65536}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN"
```
jon (sre): Putting temporary alert suppression for noisy OOM alerts while we stabilize. Will keep pager if error rates remain >5%.
ashley (runtime): Starting canary rollback of batching.lookahead change (deployment redwood-runtime-canary). If the gateway change doesn't bring error rate down we will fully rollback.
ashley (runtime): Rollback initiated: `kubectl set image deployment/redwood-runtime-canary runtime=redwood/runtime:2026-03-13`
ryan (eng-runtime): Gateway flag applied. Monitoring latency and OOMs.
jon (sre): Initial metrics: OOM rate dropped from 8.2% -> 3.0% within 90s. Token throughput decreased ~18% but error rate down. Good signal.
maria (oncall): Great. Keep the throttle until rollback completes and we can validate. Ryan, leave the flag in place and let's plan a safer rollout for the batching change.
luis (prod-eng): CS: indicate partial mitigation and that we expect further reduction after full rollback. Ask customers to retry or route to eu if urgent.
emily (support): Updated messages to top 5 customers with session IDs they provided. No escalations yet.
ashley (runtime): Canary rollback completed. Starting staged rollout to replace the bad change. Full rollout in progress with 10% -> 50% -> 100% windows.
ashley (runtime): Rollout details: reverting `batching.lookahead_ms` to 80 and re-enabling `prefetch.conservative_mode=true`.
ashley (runtime): Command used: ```
./deploy/changecfg --service runtime --set batching.lookahead_ms=80 --set prefetch.conservative_mode=true --staged
```
jon (sre): After canary rollback: OOMs down to 0.7%. Batch-size anomaly smoothed out. Graphs: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/dashboards/kvcache-oom
maria (oncall): Excellent. Leave mitigation in place for 1h and then slowly unwind gateway throttle while watching OOM and latency.
ryan (eng-runtime): I'll create an emergency guard in runtime that caps per-request prefetch tokens and enforces eviction on large prefix scans. Quick patch planned: limit_prefetch_scan = true, max_scan_tokens=20000.
ashley (runtime): We'll add a regression test in the canary pipeline to simulate extremely long prompts and ensure prefetch heuristics don't cascade.
luis (prod-eng): Action items for post-incident: - root cause doc - change control for batching flags - runbook update with emergency throttle steps - customer impact timeline
maria (oncall): I'm handing off to jon for overnight monitoring. If error rate >1% reopen pager. I'll file incident ticket and postmortem draft.\oncall handoff
maria (oncall): Handoff: jon (sre) taking over monitoring + next 2hr check. key mitigations: gateway throttle in place, batching rollback complete, rollback guard flags set.
jon (sre): Ack. I'll keep alerts on eta 1h and subscribe support channel updates. Setting dashboard snapshot in incident ticket.
emily (support): Support acked handoff and will keep customer pings going every 30m until stable.
cs-notify-bot: Updated customers.ping with mitigation note and ETA for root-cause.
maria (oncall): Postmortem owner: luis. Please collect logs for sessions with context_length > 100k and correlate with model + tenant.
luis (prod-eng): Will do. I'll also work with runtime team to add a soft cap on total KV entries per tenant to avoid cross-tenant amplification.
jon (sre): Closing active pager for now. Keeping incident open with status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update in 1h or earlier if regress. :thumbsup:
maria (oncall): Thanks team — great quick coord. We'll follow up with a blameless postmortem and action items. :eyes:
